title.narrative: Réponse à la crise alimentaire et nutritionnelle et à la situation post cyclonique pour une assistance multisectorielle éducation, protection de l’enfant et nutrition

description.narrative: The main objective of this $2m UNICEF project is to assist cyclone-affected vulnerable people in the South-East of Madagascar through a package of multisectoral assistance consisting of education for children, protection from violence, GBV and exploitation and nutritional support. To that end, UNICEF will provide treatment for 22,681 children suffering from severe acute malnutrition; provide awareness raising on best practices for infant and young child feeding, and screen children for malnutrition. Under the education component, UNICEF will provide 30,000 children at risk of school drop-out with learning materials and rehabilitate 35 classrooms with necessary roofing, and put in place 50 temporary classrooms where existing classrooms have been entirely destroyed. Under the protection component, UNICEF will protect youths from abuse by engaging them in life skills training, provide psychosocial support for cyclone-affected children and adults, provide case management for GBV survivors and strengthen the community-based protection mechanisms. In total, 30,600 people will be targeted through the education components (including 15,000 girls and 15,000 boys), 25,200 people will be reached through the child protection component (including 10,360 women and 4,200 girls), and 22,631 people will be reached through the nutrition component (including 11,089 boys and 11,542 girls).
